hook.text: In 2021, a steel pedestrian bridge was 3D-printed and installed over a canal in Amsterdam.

buildup.text: Robotic arms deposited molten steel layer by layer, guided by algorithms that optimized the shape for strength.

discovery.text: The algorithm placed material only where stress required it. The result looks organic, like a metal skeleton.

twist.text: The bridge has embedded sensors. It monitors its own stress, vibration, and temperature in real time.

climax.text: 3D printing could build bridges in remote areas using local materials, no heavy equipment required.

punchline.text: A robot printed a bridge. The bridge watches itself.

quiz.question: What is unique about Amsterdam's 3D-printed steel bridge?
options: It was printed from recycled plastic instead of metal
It has embedded sensors that monitor its own structural health
It was assembled by drones flying above the canal
